display.purpose: Masthead name only — the team on the document page, the process on a process page; uppercase, tight leading.

subhead.purpose: Drawer titles and playbook role names.

body.purpose: Prose: descriptions, drawer why-text; 11px/700 step for node titles.

label.purpose: Tabs, module titles, view buttons, filter chips; uppercase, tracked.

micro.purpose: Workhorse caption: chips, levels, stage meta, artifact labels, section labels.

shadows.name: inset-halo
shadows.purpose: White halo on the sub-process inset overlay; separates it from occluded lane content. The only shadow in the system.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: 0.28s filter dim/undim opacity transitions on lanes, edges, labels, rows.

motion.name: state-shift
motion.purpose: Washi hover wash and aria-current ink inversion on nodes, chips, view buttons.

motion.name: link-shift
motion.purpose: Process-card link hover: name and arrow go green, arrow slides 4px right. The only mark in the system that moves.

narrative.overview: A whole reading lives on one screen: a full-bleed mosaic of hairline-ruled, tabbed modules packed edge to edge, in the spirit of Japanese contemporary high-density web design. It refuses the airy sidebar-and-cards internal-tool dashboard. Nothing floats, nothing is rounded, nothing wastes a pixel; density is a feature, and the 1px gray hairline is the primary structural material. The team document is two page types cut from the same mosaic: the document page is the catalog (stat strip, one card per process, the shared catalogs as ruled row lists), and a process page is the reading of one process (no document-wide stats, a process switcher instead, and the three figures). The page is a printed process figure that happens to be interactive: every module is a numbered figure with a green tab, an uppercase title, and a right-aligned micro-caption. Ink on paper carries all content; a single utility green appears only as tabs and signals. The system encodes meaning, not decoration: dashed + stripe = open slot, ① = the single constraint, a bolt = a workflow event, a ghost pane = filtered out, a 45° hatch = an idle band; horizontal order is ordinal, never time, and rework is assumed, never drawn.
keyCharacteristics: Edge-to-edge module mosaic ruled by 1px hairlines; zero border-radius, zero decorative shadows
One compact gothic (Archivo) at a strict 56/28/16/12/10/9 scale, tabular numerals everywhere
Green (#0f6b3c) reserved for tabs and semantic signals; ink inversion is the selection voice, washi wash the hover voice
Dense micro-typography: uppercase labels, wide tracking, 9-10px captions doing real work
Every visual device is a semantic encoding readable without a legend

rules.name: The Green Is A Signal Rule
rules.body: Green never fills an area larger than a tab. It marks exactly six things: figure/section tabs, the active view, open slots, the ① constraint, workflow events, and expand/scroll affordances. A screen with green paragraphs or green panels is off-world.

rules.name: The Ink Inversion Rule
rules.body: Persistent state is spoken by inverting to solid ink with white text — aria-current selection, the active filter chip, the constraint strip. Transient hover only washes to washi; dashed open slots darken their border to ink instead, since their base is already washi. No tints, no glows, no colored highlights.

rules.name: The Strict Scale Rule
rules.body: Sizes come from 56/28/16/12/10/9 (plus the 11px node-title step). No intermediate sizes; hierarchy is carried by weight, case, and tracking.

rules.name: The Uppercase Structure Rule
rules.body: Anything that names structure — tabs, titles, labels, levels, role names, OPEN SLOT — is uppercase with letter-spacing. Explanatory prose is never uppercase.

rules.name: The Ordinal-Not-Time Rule
rules.body: Horizontal position encodes dependency order only. Nothing may imply duration, dates, or a timeline; rework loops are assumed to exist and are never drawn.

rules.name: The Shadowless Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift. If two layers must separate, use a solid 1px ink border and, for true overlays only, the white halo.

rules.name: The Semantic Texture Rule
rules.body: Dashed border + green stripe fill = open slot = the team's roadmap; 45° gray hatch = idle band; ① = the single constraint; bolt = workflow event; ghost pane = outside the current lens. These encodings are reserved — never reuse them decoratively, and never invent a second texture for a new meaning without adding it here.

dos: Do frame every new surface as a tabbed module: green tab, uppercase 10px title, 9px right-aligned meta, 1px hairline frame and internal rules.
Do speak state by ink inversion (#111111 bg, #ffffff text) and quiet hover by a washi wash; keep both at 0.12s ease-out.
Do reuse the semantic encodings exactly: dashed+stripe open slot, ① constraint, SVG bolt event, ghost pane, 45° idle hatch, 22% filter dim.
Do keep captions working: 9px uppercase micro-text with 0.04-0.1em tracking carries counts, sources, and derivations on every module.
Do let wide figures grow inside their own overflow-x: auto scroller with a green scroll hint at ≤900px; the page never scrolls horizontally.
Do divide a grid of peers (process cards, catalog rows) with a shared 1px hairline, not with borders and gaps; the seam is the divider.
Do state where a catalog entry is used in its row’s right-aligned micro tag, and say so plainly when nothing uses it ("shelf inventory", "unused", "no play yet").
donts: Don't round a corner, add a decorative shadow, or introduce a gradient; the only sanctioned shadow is the inset overlay's white halo.
Don't use green as a fill, background wash, or body-text color; it is a tab-and-signal ink only, with #7fd6a8 as its sole on-ink variant.
Don't imply time on any axis — no timelines, durations, dates, or drawn rework loops; sequence is topological order only.
Don't introduce a second typeface, an icon set, or sizes outside 56/28/16/12/10/9 (+11px node titles).
Don't float modules in whitespace or cap the page width; the mosaic runs edge to edge with only 8-10px seams of surface gray.
Don't repeat document-wide totals on a process page; a process states its own counts, and the document page owns the team's stat strip.
